ranked_baseline_findings.title: Paragraph tab-stop definitions entered the extracted text
ranked_baseline_findings.origin: Implementation follow-up; independently confirmed by reviewer
ranked_baseline_findings.concrete_case: A w:pPr/w:tabs/w:tab definition emitted a text tab because baseline handled every Word tab within the body. A separate w:r/w:tab is actual text content.

api_followup.detail: In quick-xml 0.41, deprecated unescape_value and normalized_value(Implicit1_0) delegate to identical normalized_value_with arguments: XML 1.0, depth one, predefined resolver. Both replacement calls preserve normalization and built-in entity handling; XML bytes are already validated as UTF-8.

confirmed: Regular input and length are checked before open and again through the opened handle. Input reads append from a fixed 8 KiB buffer with the input cap. No unbounded allocation from a caller-supplied document length was found.

Pinned ZipIterable parses central entries lazily and preserves duplicates for the explicit BTreeSet rejection. Initial metadata parsing does not allocate an index proportional to an attacker-declared entry count.

Bounded-input ZIP64 EOCD/locator signature rejection precedes archive construction. Header/name/comment/extra variable fields are bounded by 16-bit lengths. Remaining ZIP64 extra size values encounter entry/container/package limits before target XML is opened.

Local/central header consistency is required. Unsafe paths, duplicate decoded names, encryption, symlinks, unsupported compression, out-of-container starts/compressed sizes, excessive declared package bytes and oversized target declarations fail before extraction.
Only word/document.xml, [Content_Types].xml and _rels/.rels are opened. Other entry contents are not decompressed, resolved, executed or written to disk.

ZipReadOptions defaults retain CRC and declared-output-size checks. Crc32Reader rejects actual output beyond its declaration. The caller separately bounds actual part bytes and requires exact declared length.

Owned ZipFile drop drains a raw compressed Take reader rather than decompression/CRC. That raw reader still goes through CheckedReader and the shared I/O/cancellation budget. An early error does not initiate hidden unbounded inflation.
Requested reads and seeks are charged before cursor I/O. Borrowed UTF-8 XML events have per-event cancellation/deadline checks plus byte, depth, event, attribute, namespace and output-length caps.

DTD and processing-instruction events fail. Only predefined entities and validated numeric references resolve. No external resolver exists. Namespace additions are limited by the upstream resolver; matching end-tag validation stays enabled.
Package metadata selects one internal macro-free word/document.xml main part. Transitional and strict Word namespaces are handled. Other relationships and external targets are never fetched.

Parsing runs outside drawing and the store actor. Imports owns one Option<Job>; the result channel has capacity one. Cancellation retains the occupied slot until reaped, preventing an unbounded stream of replacement threads.

ImportCommand owns a fresh UUID, shared cancellation flag and original start time. Completion checks cancellation/time after parsing; the actor checks them again immediately before initiating the ingest call.

The UI locks the source field while busy. Explicit import cancel, generic Cancel, a newly dropped path, quit and Drop set the shared flag. A cancelled slot remains visible until its typed result arrives.
Initial command acknowledgement and later typed import completion remain separate. The UI accepts completion only for its current UUID; stale results cannot clear a newer job or overwrite its notice.

Import is a documented global library operation. Completion snapshots use the then-current actor selection; mode/session commands remain queued on that actor. Existing dirty-note protection remains in apply_snapshot.

No insertion is initiated when the final job check rejects cancellation/deadline or when extraction failed. Existing Store validation/library bounds, schema, backup/export/delete code and frozen-context behavior are unchanged.
CLI and desktop share the core reader. Existing UTF-8/Markdown bytes and attribution remain unchanged; DOCX offsets refer to exact extracted stored text.

actor_and_data_review.backup_assertion_review: The baseline test-only correction removes only exported_at from backup comparisons, first requires a positive value, then requires nondecreasing values, and still compares every other JSON field. The parent-reported earlier dynamic timestamp-equality failure remains a failed retained run, not a passing check.

documented_limits_and_boundaries: Ten-second cancellation/deadline checks are cooperative. Blocking OS metadata/open/read calls cannot be interrupted, and the one cancelled slot can remain occupied until they return. No hard wall-clock sandbox guarantee is supported.

Filesystem input symlinks are followed when their opened target is a bounded regular file; ZIP symlink entries are rejected. Size/mtime checks are best-effort change detection, not an atomic snapshot. Same-size writes with restored timestamps can evade them.

The declared package total covers all entries. Actual inflation and CRC checks cover only the three consumed parts; ignored parts are not fully integrity-validated. This is not whole-package CRC verification.

Output length is checked after appending a bounded XML event, so temporary text allocation may exceed the final 2 MiB output cap before rejection; it remains bounded by the separately capped 4 MiB XML input. Header fields can allocate up to their fixed 16-bit limits before the stricter entry-name check.
ZIP64 signatures anywhere may reject harmless matching compressed bytes. ZIP64 support is intentionally absent.

The bounded main-body profile does not reconstruct page layout, headers/footnotes/comments, hidden runs, all OOXML schemas, field evaluation, OCR or embedded content. External relationships are not fetched.
PDF remains explicitly unsupported in core, CLI, UI and contract. No PDF parser is linked.
Source tests do not establish native input/hardware, broad offline operation, model/citation/document quality or reference parity.
